findings.title: Unsafe exec() in configuration file loading allows arbitrary code execution
findings.evidence: exec() loads Python configuration without validation: exec(compile(config_file.read(), file_path, 'exec'), d.__dict__). Config sources: (1) CLI arg, (2) LEMUR_CONF env var, (3) ~/.lemur/lemur.conf.py, (4) default.conf.py.
findings.impact: Complete system compromise via arbitrary code execution if attacker controls config source.
findings.preconditions: Attacker must control one of: LEMUR_CONF env var, ~/.lemur/lemur.conf.py file, or app initialization CLI arguments in container/shared environment.
findings.recommendation: Replace exec() with importlib.import_module() or restrict config to trusted directory with strict permissions (0600). Validate file path against whitelist.
findings.verification: (1) Create malicious config in ~/.lemur/lemur.conf.py, verify it executes. (2) Check deployment docs for LEMUR_CONF usage. (3) Review container build for untrusted path sources.
traceability: CWE-95 (Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code)
CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code)

triage.reason: Environment-dependent - is LEMUR_CONF from untrusted source?
Config loading happens before auth initialization

findings.limits: Probable not confirmed because: (1) Config file origin is environment-dependent, (2) Default fallback to built-in default.conf.py is safer. Requires demonstration of path control in production environment.
findings.what_would_settle_it: Evidence of: (1) LEMUR_CONF set from untrusted source in CI/CD, (2) ~/.lemur/ world-writable in production, (3) Proof-of-concept malicious config execution

findings.title: Missing input validation on filter parameter causes IndexError
findings.evidence: Code splits filter without validation: common_name = args['filter'].split(';')[1]. No try/catch. If format is invalid (missing semicolon), raises IndexError. Test: GET /certificates/valid?filter=test returns 500.
findings.impact: Denial of Service on certificate lookup endpoint. Error leaks internal details aiding reconnaissance.
findings.recommendation: Validate format before split: parts = args['filter'].split(';'); if len(parts) < 2: return {'message': 'Invalid filter format'}, 400; common_name = parts[1]
findings.verification: (1) Authenticated user sends GET /certificates/valid?filter=nosemicolon, expects 400 not 500. (2) Handler gracefully rejects malformed input without exception.
findings.limits: Severity medium: requires authentication, affects only one endpoint, no data breach.

findings.title: Certificate upload endpoint lacks authorization gate present in creation endpoint
findings.evidence:
Two endpoints create Certificates with asymmetric authorization:

CertificatesList (POST /certificates): checks AuthorityPermission(data['authority'].id, roles).can()

CertificatesUpload (POST /certificates/upload): no AuthorityPermission check, calls service.upload(**data) directly

Both endpoints process 'authority' parameter; upload bypasses permission check.
findings.impact: BFLA - Authenticated user can upload certificates to authorities they lack permission for, bypassing authority-level access controls.
findings.preconditions: Attacker must be authenticated. Upload endpoint must be reachable.
findings.recommendation: Replicate AuthorityPermission check from CertificatesList.post() into CertificatesUpload.post(): if data.get('authority'): authority_permission = AuthorityPermission(data['authority'].id, roles); if not authority_permission.can(): return {message: '...'}, 403
findings.verification: (1) User A (Authority 1 permission) sends upload for Authority 2 - should get 403. (2) Integration test verifies upload and create enforce same authority check. (3) Diff the two handlers' authorization logic - should be identical.

triage.reason: service.upload() may have hidden auth check - need code review
This IS the FP-08 case - sibling gate asymmetry

findings.limits: Assumes upload endpoint is reachable by regular users. If service.upload() enforces authorization internally, this could drop to hardening.
findings.what_would_settle_it: Code review of lemur/certificates/service.py upload() method confirming it DOES apply authority permission check (then refute) OR DOES NOT (confirming finding).

ruled_out.where: SQLAlchemy ORM used throughout with parameterized queries (filter_by, filter(), in_() methods). No string concatenation in SQL queries. Safe ORM patterns in database.py.
Token verification enforces algorithm allowlist from config. Signature validation is mandatory. No 'none' algorithm accepted. Multiple secrets supported with strict verification.

lemur/certificates/verify.py implements _validate_revocation_url() which validates against private/loopback addresses and optional allowlist. OCSP and CRL verification properly validate URLs before requests.
No XML parsing detected in examined scope. YAML/JSON use safe libraries.
